key_insight: Training deep generative models to produce intermediate physical states (surface-current maps) instead of layouts directly yields more stable, accurate inverse design for tunable and stacked metasurfaces.
problem_solved: Directly mapping electromagnetic targets to device layouts is unstable and ill-posed for complex, tunable, or stacked metasurfaces; the paper addresses poor training stability, non-uniqueness, and difficulty incorporating physics and tunability into inverse design.
method: Learn a conditional generative model that predicts intermediate surface-current maps from desired electromagnetic responses and tuning parameters.
Use a physics-aware decoder or deterministic mapping to convert predicted current maps into physical layouts, with simulation/physics losses to enforce accuracy.
Support stacked and tunable metasurfaces by conditioning the model on layer configuration and control variables for robust multi-layer design.
impact: Provides ML practitioners a compact, physically meaningful latent representation that improves training stability, interpretability, and sample efficiency for inverse design tasks in computational electromagnetics and beyond.
